public_rationale: The February 1, 2024 study reports that shuffling answer choices in a controlled experiment changed the rankings of five of eleven models [e1]. This supports the claim that minor presentation changes can alter performance enough to reorder tested models [e1].
limitations: The study also reports less disruptive perturbations and more stable models; the effect is not universal [e1].
These benchmark results do not establish whether models have deep understanding.
February 1 is the report date; exact experiment dates are not supplied.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Minor prompt perturbations noticeably change LLM performance, enough to rearrange leaderboard rankings.
conditions: perturbations like reordering multiple choice answers, special characters, answer format changes

statement.excerpt: As it turns out, minor changes make a noticeable difference, enough to rearrange “leaderboard” rankings.

from_speaker: rearranging the order of answers in multiple choice
our_interpretation: The statement concerns controlled benchmark results available before publication, not every model or every possible perturbation.
A noticeable ranking effect means at least one reversal in the relative ordering of tested models.
The examples identify a class of changes; the claim does not require every listed change to affect every ranking.
The target is the pre-publication study record; the post gives no experiment start date.
criteria.support_condition: A contemporary controlled study finds that minor changes preserving the underlying questions alter performance enough to change model rankings.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant study reports no ranking changes, or the reported changes depend entirely on changing the questions' substantive meaning.
